cap: Iodide enters through the sodium-iodide symporter; thyroid peroxidase organifies it on thyroglobulin, and coupling MIT and DIT makes T3 while DIT plus DIT makes T4. TSH-driven endocytosis releases mostly T4, which tissue 5'-deiodinase converts to T3. A large iodide load briefly inhibits organification (Wolff-Chaikoff). Each step lists the drug that blocks it.
teach: Read left to right for synthesis and right to left for release. Severe illness reduces outer-ring deiodination, so T3 falls and reverse T3 rises. Thionamides stop new synthesis but not the release of stored hormone, which is why iodide is added in thyroid storm.
